title: SDK + API primitives for idempotent rollout manifests, scoped permission flows, and metric-driven auto-rollback
creator: Maya Chen
description: We need a first-class set of REST primitives and SDK helpers that let customers create, mutate, and observe rollout manifests (canary/A-B/shadow) in an idempotent way while enforcing scoped RBAC for who can change traffic policies. This ticket defines the API contract, SDK ergonomics, permission model, server-side idempotency semantics, and the metric-driven auto-rollback hooks that tie into Console alerts.
background: Customers frequently run progressive rollouts and experiments. Current APIs allow creating transient traffic rules but are brittle: retries can create duplicate operations, permissions are coarse-grained, and auto-rollback requires manual glue code. We must provide robust primitives so both self-serve users and enterprise teams can automate safe rollouts without building custom middleware.
goals: Define an idempotent HTTP contract for rollout operations (create/update/patch/abort)
Provide SDK helpers for manifest signing, validation, and conflict-aware retries
Design a scoped permission model (routes: rollouts:create, rollouts:approve, rollouts:promote, rollouts:abort)
Expose rollout lifecycle webhooks and metric-checkpoints to enable auto-rollback based on configured SLOs
non_goals: Designing the full Console UI for rollout flows (separate ticket)
Replacing existing classic deployment APIs immediately (we will provide compatibility adapters)
Building cross-account federation for rollouts in this iteration
acceptance_criteria: REST endpoints documented: POST /v1/projects/{pid}/rollouts (create), GET /v1/rollouts/{rid}, PATCH /v1/rollouts/{rid} (partial updates), POST /v1/rollouts/{rid}/abort, POST /v1/rollouts/{rid}/promote
Server treats client-provided idempotency-key header and returns 200 with existing rollout resource when duplicate requests are received within dedup window
SDKs (Node/Python/Go) include helpers: createRollout(manifest, opts), resumeRollout(id), abortRollout(id, reason), attachCanaryMetrics(id, metricSpec)
RBAC scope enforcement implemented: roles can be assigned per-project with minimal scopes for observers vs. operators vs. approvers
Auto-rollback trigger mechanism: user-configurable metric checks that call /v1/rollouts/{rid}/abort automatically when thresholds breached and Console shows linked alert and audit entry
Integration tests covering retry-with-idempotency, permission-denied on missing scope, and a simulated metric breach leading to rollback
api_contract_notes: Create: POST /v1/projects/{pid}/rollouts accepts a declarative 'manifest' JSON blob (traffic splits, model refs, canary windows, metricChecks). Response includes rollout_id and status = 'pending'

Idempotency: Clients must set 'Idempotency-Key' header. Server stores hash(Idempotency-Key + project_id + resource-type) for 24 hours. Duplicate create returns 200 + existing resource and original 'created_at' in body.
Update semantics: PATCH supports 'last_known_etag' header to detect concurrent edits. Bot-friendly retries should prefer POST-ing a delta manifest with idempotency key instead of blind PATCH.
Abort: POST /v1/rollouts/{rid}/abort requires 'rollouts:abort' scope and records a required 'reason' string which is surfaced in audit logs and Console timeline.
Promote: POST /v1/rollouts/{rid}/promote moves canary -> stable, requires either operator role or explicit approver approval when policy.flag 'require_human_approve' is true.
Webhooks: rollout lifecycle webhook events (rollout.created, .failed, .promoted, .aborted, .auto_rolled_back) delivered with signature header; SDKs will include verification helper
sdk_ergonomics: Manifest builder: JS/Python small DSL to build common canary templates (duration windows, traffic ramps, shadow forks)
Idempotent retry helper: sdk.retryWithIdempotency(fn, opts) that injects keys and handles 409/etag collisions transparently
Local validation: SDK validates model references, known metric names, and warns on incompatible manifest fields before sending
Event hooks: onProgress, onMetricAlert, onRollback for long-running rollout monitor usage
permission_model: Three primary scopes: rollouts.read, rollouts.write, rollouts.admin
Fine-grained actions: 'create' requires rollouts.write, 'promote' may require rollouts.admin depending on project policy, 'abort' allowed for write by default but can be locked to admin

Approval flow: createRollout can be staged in 'awaiting_approval' state when policy requires human approve; approvers must have role 'rollout:approver' mapped to rollouts.admin or a separate 'rollouts.approve' scope
Audit requirements: every change to rollout state must include actor id, source (SDK/API/Console), and optional justification string stored for 180 days
idempotency_edge_cases: Duplicate create within dedup window should return the same rollout_id and original created_at; if original request failed after server performed partial side-effects, server must attempt cleanup or mark as 'orphaned' and include remediation instructions

Long-running operations: idempotency keys for create should be valid for the entire canary duration (configurable by project upto 7 days) to allow safe client retries during intermittent network issues

Cross-client collisions: if two different clients issue different manifests but same idempotency key, we will compare payload hashes and return 409 if mismatch with clear error message including original request fingerprint
auto_rollback_design: Metric checks: manifest can declare metricChecks: [{metricName, direction, threshold, aggregation, evaluationWindow, gracePeriod}]

Evaluation engine: rollout controller polls metric backends (Prometheus/Kafka metrics adapter) and evaluates checks at configured cadence; when threshold breached and gracePeriod expired, controller transitions rollout to 'auto_rolled_back' and invokes abort pathway

Safety net: before auto-rollback finalizes, controller attempts a protected cool-off (default 1 minute) and sends webhook + Console notification; allow manual override to 'force_promote' within cooldown
Observability: every evaluation step recorded as timeline event with metric values, and linked to trace IDs for debugging
testing_plan: Unit tests for idempotency behavior and etag concurrency handling
Integration test simulating network retries during rollout create and ensuring single resource recorded
E2E scenario: canary with metric check that breaches after 3 minutes causing auto-rollback; verify webhook and audit entries
Permission matrix tests to assert expected 403s and 2xx for scope combinations
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: idempotency window can lead to stale keys occupying storage; Mitigation: TTL + compacted store and allow admin cleanup endpoints
Risk: metric noise causing frequent auto-rollbacks; Mitigation: require gracePeriod and support multiple metric aggregations (p95,p99,rate) and allow manual whitelists
Risk: exposing powerful abort/promote endpoints to too many users; Mitigation: default conservative roles and enable org policy restrictions per-project
implementation_notes: Server: add RolloutIdempotency table indexed by project_id + idempotency_key_hash with payload_fingerprint + rollout_id + created_at + ttl
Controller: reuse existing deployment reconciler (ENG-24168) with new metric-check hooks and timeline event API
SDK: provide helpers in next minor release across Node/Python/Go; follow semver minor with feature flag default off for early access
Console: wire timeline, webhook settings, and approval flows in a follow-up UI ticket
